title: How to Use the Months Before a Medallia or Qualtrics Renewal
summary: Start six months before your Medallia or Qualtrics renewal: audit usage, test on your own data, then decide to keep, add an analytics layer or replace.
body_markdown:
Most CX teams notice their Medallia or Qualtrics renewal when the paperwork arrives. By then, the only real choice left is to sign. Changing your CX stack, or adding to it, is cheap in the months before a renewal and expensive at almost any other time. Mid-term, a change means paying for two things at once. At renewal, it means choosing what you pay for next.


Use that window for a structured decision, not a negotiation tactic. Start about six months out. Audit what the team actually uses, run a side-by-side test on your own feedback, then choose one of three outcomes: keep the incumbent as is, keep it and add a specialized analytics layer such as Thematic, or replace it. Keeping the incumbent is often the right call. The window lets you make that call on evidence, not by default.


Below is a five-stage timeline, a worked example, and the mistakes that waste the window.


## The five-stage renewal timeline


1. **Six months out: audit what you actually use.** Channels, themes, integrations and seats.
2. **Four to five months out: name the question and the people.** Decide what problem a change would solve, and who has to agree.
3. **90 to 120 days out: run a side-by-side on your own data.** Test the current analysis against an alternative on the same feedback.
4. **60 days out: decide keep, add or replace.** Pick one outcome and write down why.
5. **30 days out: renew on what you learned.** Bring usage and test results into the renewal conversation.


Zylo's[renewal guide](https://zylo.com/blog/guide-saas-renewal) recommends setting "alerts at 120, 90, 60, and 30 days." This timeline starts earlier, because the audit and the test take longer than a procurement review.


## Step 1: Six months out, audit what you actually use


The audit answers one question: what does the team pay for, and what does it rely on? Four checks cover most of it.


- **Channels.** Count every place feedback arrives: surveys, support tickets, reviews, app store comments, chat and call transcripts. Then count how many the platform analyzes today. The gap between those two numbers is the most useful figure in the audit.
- **Defensible themes.** Pick your five most-reported themes. For each, ask whether someone can show a skeptical executive exactly which customer comments sit behind it. A theme no one can defend won't survive a boardroom disagreement.
- **Integration ownership.** List every data flow into and out of the platform, and name the person who owns each one.[BCG's 2025 applications research](https://www.bcg.com/publications/2025/seven-questions-smarter-applications-strategy) found that the strongest predictor of integration success is internal IT capability, not vendor choice.
- **Seats and modules.** Compare licensed seats and modules against active use. Zylo's[2026 SaaS Management Index](https://zylo.com/news/2026-saas-management-index) found that organizations leave an average of 36% of their SaaS licenses unused. The audit tells you whether your CX platform follows that pattern.


Audit usage, not features. The question isn't what the platform can do. It's what your team does with it every week.


## Step 2: Four to five months out, name the question and the people


The audit usually surfaces one of two problems. Either the team isn't getting enough from what it already has, or the analysis can't answer the questions stakeholders ask. These lead to very different renewals.


If the problem is adoption, the fix is training, configuration or fewer seats. If it's analysis, write the unanswered questions down in plain language. "Why did net promoter score (NPS) drop in the Northeast last quarter?" is a testable question. "We need better insights" is not.


Then map who has to agree: CX, insights, IT, procurement and finance, each wanting a different artifact. Thematic's guide on[how to get buy-in for a new customer feedback platform](https://getthematic.com/insights/get-buy-in-customer-feedback-platform) covers the buying group. Identify every approver now, not 30 days out.


## Step 3: 90 to 120 days out, run a side-by-side on your own data


Most teams skip this step. It's the one that makes the decision defensible. Take a real export of your feedback and run it through the current platform's analysis and through an alternative. Compare the results on the questions you wrote down in Step 2.


Both incumbents document how to get your data out. Qualtrics lets you[export all participants' responses](https://www.qualtrics.com/support/survey-platform/data-and-analysis-module/data/download-data/export-data-overview/) in formats including CSV and SPSS. Medallia's[Query API documentation](https://developer.medallia.com/medallia-apis/docs/extract-survey-responses-for-offline-analysis-data-warehousing) states that raw data "can be extracted from Experience Cloud for archiving in data warehouses." A side-by-side needs no contract change and doesn't touch the live program.


Judge the comparison on two things. First, consistency: if the alternative's themes line up with what your current analysis already shows, you can trust its method. Second, depth: whether it surfaces more specific drivers than the current analysis, the kind a team can act on. Consistency builds confidence. Added depth is what justifies a change.


Give the test enough time. Loading a real export, scoring the results and getting stakeholders to review them takes weeks, not days. That is why this step starts at 90 to 120 days. For the scoring itself, Thematic's guide on[how to evaluate an AI feedback analytics platform during a proof of concept](https://getthematic.com/insights/evaluate-ai-feedback-analytics-poc) covers accuracy, traceability and time-to-value.


## Step 4: 60 days out, decide keep, add or replace


By now, the audit and the test should point at one of three outcomes.


**Outcome** **Choose it when** **What changes at renewal**


Keep as is Feedback is mostly one survey program, the built-in analysis answers stakeholder questions, and the problems found were adoption problems Right-size seats and modules; nothing else


Keep and add an analytics layer Collection, alerting and case management work well, but feedback arrives from more channels than the platform analyzes, or themes can't be defended Incumbent stays for collection and action; a specialized layer handles analysis


Replace The platform no longer fits collection or action needs, and someone can own a migration Plan the switch before the notice deadline


Keeping the incumbent is a legitimate result. Medallia's[platform](https://www.medallia.com/platform/) bundles feedback capture, alerting and case management. If your bottleneck is following up with unhappy customers, the incumbent is built for that job.


Adding a layer answers a narrower problem.[Forrester noted in December 2025](https://www.forrester.com/blogs/introducing-the-new-customer-feedback-management-and-analytics-solutions-market/) that "surveys and dashboards have become mostly commoditized and aren't driving buying decisions." Analysis is where teams usually feel the gap. Thematic is built for that one[analytics layer](https://getthematic.com/insights/cx-stack-feedback-analytics-layer) , and it sits on top of an existing survey platform rather than replacing it. If you choose to replace instead, the Thematic guide on[how to migrate off Medallia or Qualtrics without losing your feedback history](https://getthematic.com/insights/migrate-off-medallia-qualtrics) covers exports, parallel runs and cutover.


Count the cost of two vendors, too. BCG found that 39% of best-of-breed adopters spend more than 20% of their IT budget on integration, against 29% of suite users. If Step 1 found no integration owner, weigh that heavily.


## Step 5: 30 days out, renew on what you learned


The last month is for paperwork, not discovery. The work from Steps 1 to 4 now does two jobs.


First, it sets the scope: seats, modules and channels should match what the audit found. Second, it gives the conversation substance. A team with usage data, test results and a written decision negotiates from evidence. A team that only says "we're looking at alternatives" doesn't.


Check the notice period in your contract before this stage. Many enterprise agreements auto-renew unless notice is given by a set date. That date can fall well before the renewal itself. Thematic's migration guide recommends starting 90 to 120 days before a contract auto-renews for exactly this reason. If your notice deadline is early, move every step in this timeline earlier to match.


## A worked example: keeping the platform and adding a layer


A common outcome of this process is the middle row of the table. The incumbent keeps doing what it does well: collecting feedback across locations and journey points, plus alerting and case management. A specialized analytics layer such as Thematic discovers themes and ties them to NPS impact. A BI tool can distribute the results. Nothing is ripped out.


[Community Health System](https://getthematic.com/insights/community-health-systems-actionable-insights) , a not-for-profit healthcare network, kept its PG Forsta survey program and added Thematic to analyze open-ended employee engagement comments. The team produced 250 one-page department reports in three days. Analysis time fell from about 250 hours to about 83 hours per cycle. "Before, we were doing everything in an Excel spreadsheet," said Alexandra Clifton, Organizational Development Partner.


## Common mistakes to avoid


- **Starting at 30 days.** There is no time left to test anything. Start the audit six months out.
- **Treating the window as a bluff.** A real evaluation looks different from a pressure tactic. Run a real side-by-side, or don't claim one.
- **Testing on vendor demo data.** Curated samples tell you little. Use an export of your own feedback.
- **Assuming change is the goal.** Keeping the incumbent is often right. The goal is a decision you can defend.
- **Ignoring integration ownership.** A second tool with no owner underperforms its demo. Name the owner before you choose to add.
- **Missing the notice deadline.** Auto-renewal terms can close the window early. Read the contract in Step 1, not Step 5.


Open your contract this week and find two dates: the renewal date and the notice deadline. Count back six months from the earlier one. That's when the audit starts.
